title: AHU-1 Freezestat Trip During Occupied Cooling
description: AHU-1 is running normally in cooling mode when the real physical freezestat safety switch trips, exactly as it would from a real low mixed-air-temperature condition on the bench.

events.description: Run AHU-1 throughout the baseline and trip
Establish a real chilled-water coil load
Create an occupied terminal airflow request
Trip the freezestat interlock via a real BACnet write -- WebCTRL sees the same trip WebCTRL reads that the equipment model reacts to

expected_results: AHU-1 Supply Air Temperature rises as the heating valve is forced open by the interlock
The AHU's internal fan-running state drops even if WebCTRL is still commanding SA Fan SS on
WebCTRL should show a Freezestat Trip alarm and command AHU-1 to a safe shutdown state
Discharge temp downstream at VAV-1/VAV-2 should stop tracking normal cooling behavior
completion_criteria: Student correctly identifies the freezestat trip as the root cause, not a valve or fan failure
Student verifies the trip by reading the Freezestat Trip point directly rather than guessing from symptoms alone
instructor_notes: The 120-second baseline allows chiller proof, CHW transport, fan proof, and cooling-coil thermal lag to become visible before the trip. Scenario conditions remain active after the final event; use STOP to relinquish only this lesson or RESET to clear every instructor fault/force.
student_objectives: Diagnose a safety interlock trip using only WebCTRL's available points, not this admin tool
Explain why a freezestat forces heating open and disables the fan rather than just alarming
